steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Traditional British dishes include: roast beef and Yorkshire pudding, fish and chips, shepherd's pie, full English breakfast, Sunday roast, and trifle.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: British cuisine has been significantly influenced by immigration and global trade: Indian, Chinese, Italian, Caribbean, and Middle Eastern foods are now part of everyday British eating.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Chicken tikka masala is often described as a British national dish, reflecting the fusion of Indian cooking with British tastes.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Key international cuisines and their staples: Italian (pasta, olive oil, tomatoes), Indian (rice, spices, lentils, ghee), Chinese (rice, soy sauce, stir-frying), Mexican (tortillas, beans, chillies), Thai (rice, coconut, lemongrass).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name three traditional British dishes. | Q: How has multiculturalism changed the British diet? | Q: What are the staple foods of Indian cuisine?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Roast beef and Yorkshire pudding, fish and chips, shepherd's pie, full English breakfast, Sunday roast, trifle, Cornish pasty (any three). | Multiculturalism has introduced new ingredients, recipes, and cooking techniques from around the world, expanded supermarket ranges, created diverse restaurant options, and led to fusion cuisine. Chic | Rice, lentils (dahl), spices (cumin, coriander, turmeric), ghee, and flatbreads (naan, chapatti).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When asked about British cuisine, give specific named dishes, not just vague descriptions. Link multiculturalism to specific cuisines and how they changed British eating habits (e.g. Indian cuisine led to the popularity of curry). Use the term 'fusion cuisine' when describing dishes that combine culinary traditions. For higher marks, explain the historical reasons behind food influences (immigration, trade, empire).
